steps.text: ...Allerdale, it's no good habit to eavesdrop. Listen to your father, now.
Only lowly scoundrels would hide away in the dark to plot the demise of another.
Maybe they do it for their own benefit, but such stolen victories never last for long.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: (Urgh... lowly scoundrels, both of them...)
She doesn't want to be caught barefaced, especially not by these awful people. It'd disappoint her father, and bring shame on the Cumberland name.
If she can just climb out of the window...

steps.name: Indistinct Officer
steps.text: We need to seize the moment.

steps.name: Indistinct Officer
steps.text: The soldiers are counting heads right now. We'll mingle with the crowd in the confusion. That way, nobody will realize we were ever gone.

steps.name: Obscured Merchant
steps.text: ...Did you hear something?

steps.name: Indistinct Officer
steps.text: It must be some little house pest. Don't overthink it. How's a room so cramped going to hide anyone?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Phew...
She carefully, gingerly cowers inside the shadow. Her most loyal ally—the tremendous suit of steam armor—becomes her shield.
Her fingers feel to the edge of the window, and if she can just climb over and out, she can avoid this duo's line of sight, and climb down the gutter pipe.
Her skirt's filthy by now. Ailshie won't be happy about this.
But as long as she's not caught...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Agh!
She doesn't understand what happened.

The sky and ground seem to spin before her eyes, the inside of Allerdale's head whirling with. Her hands and legs lose all purchase, her grasp and footing touch nothing but thin air. She plummets straight from the second story.
The garden scenery screams like mad towards her head, but before she hits the stiff soil, a soft yet ample cushion catches her.
A cushion from where?
No, it's not even a cushion.
Allerdale feels herself gently placed upon the ground.
She turns to looks behind—
And creatures confined to legend stand before her.
They must have leapt out of a fairy tale just a moment ago, stood there imposingly in the garden. They really do exist.
Their golden fur gleams scintillant as the sun. The one at the head has pupils of deep brown, and they are now calmly staring at Allerdale.
Allerdale, brought by her father, has had several audiences with His Majesty, and seen generations of portraits of the Aslan kings hung on the palace walls.
But this is the first time she cannot help the urge to bow her head before such a gaze—for the ones before her seem more awe-inspiring than any monarch.

Yet a Cumberland does not bow so lightly. Allerdale makes a conscious effort to keep her head held high, as high as it can go, and only then does she notice that the one in the center carries a human astride him.
A girl who must be even younger than her, dressed in sumptuous ceremony, languidly sat atop his back akin to plated gold.
In his mouth is held a sword... a sword that outsizes the girl by far.
A deep, resonant voice arises in Allerdale's head.

a.text: You will meet Vina again, someday.'

steps.text: This is the first time Allerdale meets them, and the last as well.
In the over twenty years to follow, this sight will recur in her dreams, dreams of that august, golden presence, of the girl who was there with them—
Until, like the Aristocrat of Beasts prophesized, she once again meets the one named Vina.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Look, that... that's...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Her Royal Highness Alexandrina!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Inform His Majesty immediately, we've found Her Highness, she's in the garden right this moment—

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Wait, I'm not seeing things, am I? Isn't that... the missing...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Her Highness—she's found the Sighs of Kings!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: God save Victoria!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: God save the King!
Cheers instantly erupt throughout the garden.
Servicemen, nobles, servants... everyone swarms for the place, eyes on Her Highness bearing the symbol of royal power.
What a miracle it is!
Hot tears fill the people's eyes, and one after another they reach their hands out in joy.

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: Miss Allerdale... what are you doing here?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: ...Ailshie.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: You can't see them?

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: Them? Who do you mean? Her Highness Alexandrina?

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: She's the only one there, you know.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No, them, they're golden...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: He just said something to me too.

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: Did something happen to you? Your skirt's dirty to high heaven... are you alright?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I... I'm not sure.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Stars... stars fell into the room upstairs.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: The steam knight... armor... it gave those scoundrels a beating!

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: I don't understand what you're telling me.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Ailshie, I feel really dizzy.

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: You need some proper rest. Who hasn't lost their head, seeing all of this? Far too much has happened today.

steps.name: Noble Lady
steps.text: Did you see? Her Royal Highness Alexandrina came back with the missing Sighs of Kings!

steps.name: Noble Gentleman
steps.text: The cheers from the gardens were practically shaking all the windows and walls. Hardly anyone believed their own eyes. Her Highness Alexandrina in the flesh—and her age, how young is she still?

steps.name: Noble Lady
steps.text: 'A miracle,' everyone's calling it.

steps.name: Noble Gentleman
steps.text: Yes, a miracle, of course it is.

steps.name: Noble Gentleman
steps.text: The greatest difference between miracles and coincidence is that miracles never descend for no reason in the time and place they do.

steps.name: Noble Gentleman
steps.text: It'll be His Majesty's birthday soon... How could I not consider this magical affair a splendid portent of things to come?

steps.name: Noble Lady
steps.text: Do give that a rest. They put on this whole auteur-styled drama for the merriment of anyone watching.

steps.name: Noble Lady
steps.text: What I'm suddenly minding is the opinion some dukes have of His Majesty and our Duke of Cumberland...

steps.name: Noble Gentleman
steps.text: Leave it there. All worries on the backburner, now. The dinner party's about to begin.

steps.name: Noble Lady
steps.text: You're quite right. Let's enjoy everything here to the fullest—

steps.name: Noble Gentleman & Noble Lady
steps.text: God save Victoria!

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: ...It seems the people's attentions are on Alexandrina's adventure.

steps.name: Sullen Voice
steps.text: Your Majesty... you knew beforehand Her Highness would enter the cavern underground?

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: It was a fine opportunity. With me out of the Palace, the diligent guards could more easily chatter, or perhaps sleep on the job, and thus let this little intruder of ours slip by.

steps.name: Sullen Voice
steps.text: So you planned all this.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: Half was his fine improvisation. He does like a harmless little practical joke on us humans now and then.

steps.name: Sullen Voice
steps.text: If he went along with this, does that imply he, too, considered this a necessary deed?

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: ...Londinium will be soon for summer. Awfully stuffy days, and torrents of rain from time to time. You're planning to send Allerdale and the wife out of the city yourself, aren't you?

steps.name: Sullen Voice
steps.text: Your Majesty! My intention has always been but one, I simply...

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: Robert, you adore your daughter, as do I.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: We are to wager everything for Victoria's present, but they are Victoria's future. On the off-chance we do fail...

spans.text: We are to wager everything for Victoria's present, but they are Victoria's future. On the off-chance we

steps.name: Sullen Voice
steps.text: We will not, Your Majesty. I will ensure the worst case does not happen, if it takes my very life.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: I'm filled with great courage and confidence at our prospects. Still, it doesn't hinder me from planning just the most minute escape option for Alexandrina.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: She'll be ruling Victoria sooner or later. Is it so wrong to have her get to grips with this city in advance?

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: And a similar farce still more or less served to right the balance, on this stifling-seeming afternoon.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: Under all this pressure, the people's spirits need a little boost. That is what we're met here for.

spans.text: Under all this pressure, the people's spirits need a little boost.
is what we're met here for.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: Of course... we all have some premonition. Hence why we made these calculations, correct?

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: Come, Robert. Once you're done with your tea, we'll be due downstairs.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I hear music. That's the band Dad and His Majesty invited?

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: Yes, Miss Allerdale. The dinner party's about to begin.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Everyone's so happy.

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: Aren't you, too?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Ailshie... will the days go on like this forever?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Me and you, and Dad, and Mum... we'll always be together?

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: I don't know, Miss Allerdale. But I believe nothing ever stays completely the same, just as the flowers in the garden.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No. There are some things that will never change, Ailshie!

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'll grow up to be a Steam Knight, just like Sir Lynch! No, even greater than Sir Lynch!

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'll protect you all, and I'll drive every scoundrel away.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'll uphold the glory of Cumberland, just like my great-great-great-great grandmother!

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I promise this, Ailshie! You'll see!

steps.name: Maid Ailshie
steps.text: Miss...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: ...I'm not leaving Londinium. You're not allowed to leave either, Ailshie.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm going to tell Dad—

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: This is my home. Just like every Cumberland's done before me, I'll keep it, I'll protect it, until my life is over.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I swear.
